## Exact concrete theorem and application

Namespace: `YulangClosure.NativeLocalDecodeR60`.

```lean
concrete_local_decode (n : ProviderNativeContextR57.Native S T)
  (search : ProviderNativeContextR57.Search S T) (policy : Policy T) :
  ReachedSlotSearchR58.LocalDecode (constructedReaders n policy)
    (ProviderNativeContextR57.inputs n search)
```

There is **no supplied LocalDecode, StepReads, reader-soundness, Owned,
FaithfulExtraction, or existing model Inputs/Context argument**. Native n is
the existing primitive owner record, not an unexplained Context. R57.inputs
and every reader are computed from that same n. The source inventory's keys,
raw endpoint constructors, state tags and original indexes remain explicit.
The complete exact theorem types and transitive axioms appear below.

Policy contains only the intentionally separate Internal/ancestry callbacks.
Rows, views and physical are constructed from n; their correctness is independent
of those callbacks (`physical_reader_independent_of_policy`). This does not
pretend to construct or verify the actual Rust Internal/ancestry visitor.
Its source simulation and resource interpretation remain separate obligations.

`constructed_candidate_iff` instantiates the full R59 successful initial-Run
candidate equivalence for these readers. `complete_candidates_on_constructed_inputs`
applies the same R59 converse and the existing consumer refinement, supplying
`concrete_local_decode` internally. For an actual initial successful Run and
original Checked terminal branch it derives result membership,
R49.pathCheck=true and R49.Arrival in **inputs n search**, with no extra decoder
assumption. It does not assert successful Run existence, native execution,
R57 legacy path-table equality, complete authentication or whole hygiene.

## Primitive construction and why this is not an assumed law

| Component | Actual construction and proof |
| --- | --- |
| rows | `rowRead` selects the unique same-state raw index from n.effectRows; `rows` returns that raw four-vector bounds record. `row_reader_projection`, `current_row_slot` and `current_atom_slot` derive R47.currentBound from these exact owner/vector/getElem reads. Canonical representative is retained by the Native row but never substituted for the raw requested index. |
| views | `viewRead` selects the unique same-state original index from the full n.views inventory. `view_reader_projection` proves owner/index and existing R48 view equality. `support_reads_from_view_inventory` derives supportView, indexed view, exact native member, ordered family and closed-tail equations from this one read. It uses the existing LocalDecode field's closed-tail/member premises, rather than inventing a physical emission for Support. |
| target | `targetRead` reads the actual row slot. Row lane constructs EffectEndpoint.row; atom lane rejects EffectEndpoint.row as BoundMismatch before emission lookup. Accepted TargetRead.current is proved from actual raw vector reads; it is not an assumed currentBound law. |
| physical | `matching` enumerates all emissions with their original indexes and exact encoded physical slot. `indexed_filter_projection`/`matching_selected` prove index round-trip and singleton physical-slot inventory against the same R47 current projection. `checkPhysical` performs source-order validation and constructs a proof-carrying PhysicalRead receipt only on success. |
| physical field proof | `physical_receipt_decodes` derives every R48.EdgeReads conjunct and exact next endpoint from those local facts. `relation_read_live` derives live relation membership from the same-state indexed relation record. `concrete_local_decode` obtains a receipt by case analysis of actual checkPhysical success and discharges the physical LocalDecode field. It does not accept a receipt or a soundness law as a theorem input. |

TargetRead/PhysicalRead are **outputs of the checking functions**. Their fields
are facts established by actual native row/index/emission/readback/admission/
relation checks. Merely defining those structures would prove nothing; the
concrete decoder theorem explicitly uses their constructed success branch.
No runtime guard calls StepReads, EdgeReads or LocalDecode to make itself true.
All compared R47 fields are explicit R57 conversions of the retained primitive
native records, not an arbitrary supplied model table.

`checkPhysical` order is: current row/index and atom-row guard; exact caller-cell
target reconciliation; no/one/multiple matching emissions; emission/current/
readback equality; indexed admission presence and bound; relation presence;
exact live relation pair. Duplicate slot emissions reject before stale-readback
inspection. Internal or ancestry validation never runs in the physical reader.
The physical result has no invented ancestry witness (its list is empty);
Entry policy remains in the original R58 policy layer and order.

The model physical callback takes an explicit Cell.target, so it also reconciles
that value with the re-read slot. The Rust API physical_lower(row,lane,index)
computes its target itself; model Cell.target comes from the same rows reader
in actual worklist expansions. Arbitrary forged Cells are rejected by the model
reconciliation. No full Rust-to-Run argument for that alignment is claimed.

## Source map and guard scope

Frozen source constructors:
`ProviderNativeContextProjection::local_decode_reader`, `LocalDecodeReader`,
`LocalDecodeReader::{row,view,physical_lower}` in `candidate_receiver.rs`
(around2645–2704 and following). Their owning projections are the complete
R55 row/representative inventory and R57 view inventory, retained session,
exact live State, and their pointer/index round trips. The physical helper is
unchanged `candidate_context.rs:3069–3102` (`checked_physical_lower_edge`).
R47.currentBound and R48.EdgeReads are the exact audited definitions, not new
weakened versions.

The new private Rust atom-row guard is represented exactly: R47 maps every
atom-vector element through an effectAtom key, while a raw EffectRow constructor
would encode as effectRow. That case now yields unavailable from the sealed
R60 reader. This changes neither existing certified_lower_paths nor forwarding,
producers or the original supported source domain. R60 does not claim that
all existing native search executions can use the new observer successfully.
Malformed observer inputs remain unavailable; the original source cases stay
in their separate parent obligations.

View reads intentionally retain open tails; the original search guard rejects
such a view before member enumeration. Moving the tail error into unrelated
view lookup or moving ancestry into physical would alter failure order; neither
was done. Raw and canonical row coordinates remain separate.

## Required falsifiers and accepted finite witnesses

- Foreign model state tags, swapped physical lane/index, stale readback,
  duplicate slot emissions and wrong relation pair each have exact rejected
  readPhysical equations. Duplicate-before-stale priority is witnessed.
- Canonical40 cannot substitute for original raw row4; the physical raw4 read
  still succeeds. Crossed state/index view records remain unavailable.
- A retained old Support member/family/view is rejected after member order
  changes; the original ordinal is not replaced by an equality search.
- Atom-lane EffectRow is rejected before both missing-emission and duplicate-
  emission cases. This exercises the newly admitted guard and priority.
- `open_support_tail_rejected_at_search_guard` is a complete initial search
  Run to MissingCommonEndpoint after the original pop charge and view read.
- `concrete_physical_and_policy_separation` shows successful physical reads
  can coexist with a failing first Internal policy; the reader does not call
  ancestry early. Generic policy-independence is also proved.
- `concrete_rows_views_and_decoder` instantiates the full constructed decoder
  on the existing R57 fixture Native/search. These are finite model witnesses,
  not Rust runtime tests or a successful forwarding/publication claim.

Foreign-tag fixtures distinguish different model state tags. Rust rejects
foreign object pointers through the sealed owner checks; an injective/common
interpretation of those pointers as Lean Nat tags has **not** been proved.
